newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Kartonsan expects 7.5-8 trln lira 97 turnover.
newsitem.headline: Turk Kartonsan expects 7.5-8 trln lira 97 turnover.

text.p: Turkey's leading white-lined chipboard and triplex board producer Kartonsan Karton Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. expects 1997 turnover to rise to 7.5 to eight trillion lira in current prices from five to 5.5 trillion lira expected in 1996, a senior company official said.

"Our total sales in 1997 should be between 7.5 to eight trillion lira in current prices. But this can occur if current conditions continue," Salih Cetinsoy, assistant general manager of the company, told Reuters.
Kartonsan shares traded at 10,000 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange on Tuesday, down slightly from Monday's 10,250 close.
The company completed a capacity expansion investment this year to raise total yearly capacity to 160,000 tonnes from previous 130,000 tonnes.
"During the investment, we had temporary production stoppages. That is why we could not meet our seven trillion lira turnover target for 1996," Cetinsoy said.
But the management is hopeful for 1997, because of the capacity expansion, automation and modernisation investments which significantly lowered production costs.
"We became more competitive and profitable in both domestic and international markets," Cetinsoy said.

Kartonsan reported a 3.76 trillion lira turnover in the first nine months of 1996, slightly less than 3.88 trillion in the same 1995 period. But its nine-month net profit soared to 2.11 trillion lira from previous 1.50 trillion lira.
The company's 1996 exports are estimated at 10,000 tonnes and more than $6 million in value and the 1997 targets are 15,000 tonnes and $8-9 million.
Kartonsan will start to produce a new product called "carrier board" to the domestic market in 1997.

"We will begin production in the first quarter. We hope to substitute imports in the domestic market and to export the rest of the output because there is strong demand abroad for this type of board," Cetinsoy said.
The domestic board market is 160,000 tonnes and is expected to grow by four percent next year to 167,000 tonnes.
"Last year we were controlling 75 percent of the market with (state-owned) Seka having five percent and European producers the rest," Cetinsoy said.

"Immediately after the duties were lifted, the European producers rushed into the Turkish market with price discounts of up to 15 percent which caused us to lose a five percent market share to them," he added.
Turkey lifted all custom duties for European industrial goods and services on January 1, 1996, as part of a customs union agreement with the European Union.
Kartonsan also began to ponder deeply on its new investment plans after the effects of the customs pact.
"Because the EU producers have been losing their Fareast markets due to new investments in that region, they began to dump their excess output on the easiest market, Turkey," Cetinsoy said.
"If we decide to go ahead with the new investment, the new line will at least have a yearly capacity of 130,000 tonnes, to be able to compete," he added.
A second private producer Kombassan is to enter the domestic market with a 30,000-tonne capacity in late 1997.

"But despite the rise in imports, European producers are not that active in the domestic market and we began making all our plans according to the conditions in the European market which comprises Turkey (after the customs union)," Cetinsoy said.
